issues.title: Unsupported Barron-to-H1 compactness

failure_location.quote: Any bounded sequence in Barron space $\mathcal{B}_1$ has a subsequence that converges in $H^1(\Omega)$

issues.failure_explanation: The proof combines the continuous embedding B1 into H1 with the compact embedding H1 into L2. Those facts imply that a B1-bounded sequence has an L2-convergent subsequence, not an H1-convergent subsequence. No separate H1-compactness argument is supplied.
issues.overall_effect: The H1 convergence conclusion in main and the H1 conclusion for the representation-cost regularizer in main2 are not established by the old compactness argument.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace Lemma convergesubsq by the valid statement that every bounded sequence in B1 or H1 has an L2-convergent subsequence. Restate the regularization conclusion of main and the representation-cost branch of main2 as L2 convergence, and conduct their compactness and contradiction arguments in L2. The finite-stopping and network-width estimates can remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The cited embeddings yield only L2 compactness, so the two H1 conclusions cannot remain on the old argument. Downgrading them to L2 gives a complete, contained repair and leaves recognizable regularization theorems, but it meaningfully loses derivative-level convergence in both affected results. That limited weakening makes the issue moderate rather than minor or serious.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: Any bounded sequence in Barron space $\mathcal{B}_1$ or Sobolev space $H^1(\Omega)$ has a subsequence that converges in $L^2(\Omega)$.

issues.title: ENN2 requires eventual radius inclusion

failure_location.quote: On the other hand, by the definition of $r(n)$, we have $r(n)\to +\infty$

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $r:=r(n)$ be a monotonic increasing function

issues.failure_explanation: A positive monotone radius may remain bounded. If its limiting radius is below the representation cost needed for the exact solution, the approximants supplied by the approximation theorem never belong to X_{n,r(n)}. Thus the finite-stopping argument proves the theorem only under an additional eventual-inclusion condition, not under the stated old assumptions.
issues.overall_effect: The old well-posedness and finite-stopping assertion for ENN2 is unsupported for admissible bounded radius maps, contrary to the accompanying claim that no additional condition on r is needed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require the radius sequence in main2 to be nondecreasing and to satisfy r(n) tending to infinity. Equivalently, the proof minimally needs eventual inclusion of the approximation class X_{n,cρ(f†)} in X_{n,r(n)}. Include the resulting fixed inclusion threshold in the stopping proof; it does not alter the asymptotic width or iteration estimates.
issues.why_classification: The repair is local and preserves the ENN2 method, conclusions, and rates, but it excludes the coherent bounded monotone radius maps expressly allowed by the old statement and contradicts the accompanying assertion that no additional condition on r is needed. This is a limited but substantive restriction of the algorithm's input contract, so it is moderate.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: Let $r:\mathbb N\to(0,\infty)$ be a nondecreasing sequence satisfying $r(n)\to+\infty$ as $n\to\infty$.

issues.title: ENN2 existence lacks lower semicontinuity of the regularizer
issues.failure_explanation: Local Hölder continuity of R1 at f-dagger does not imply continuity or lower semicontinuity at arbitrary points of X_{n,r(n)}. Compactness of the feasible class alone therefore does not justify the asserted Weierstrass minimizer. Without attainment, the algorithm and both conclusions of main2 are not well-defined for the full stated regularizer class.
issues.overall_effect: The old theorem does not establish existence of each ENN2 minimizer for the R1 branch, so finite stopping and convergence of the generated sequence are unsupported there.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add that the R1 regularizer is sequentially weakly lower semicontinuous in H1(Ω). For a minimizing sequence, use coercivity to obtain an H1 bound, extract a weakly H1-convergent and strongly L2-convergent subsequence, use L2-closedness of the fixed feasible class, and apply lower semicontinuity to obtain a minimizer. The remainder of main2 then proceeds unchanged.
issues.why_classification: Local Hölder continuity at f† does not supply the lower semicontinuity needed for attainment, so this is substantive rather than a typo. Nevertheless, weak lower semicontinuity is a standard direct-method qualification satisfied by the intended H1-norm regularizer, and adding it requires only a routine local existence argument without changing the algorithm, convergence topology, stopping rate, or intended regular regime. The issue is therefore minor.

issues.title: Tikhonov coefficient-cost sublevels are not controlled
issues.failure_explanation: The proof infers a finite representation-cost radius from a bounded value of varphi. The old A2 is also ill-typed, declaring varphi on the network class although it is applied to a scalar cost. Even after the evident scalar correction, a function such as 1-exp(-t) is continuous and increasing but bounded, so a bounded varphi(c) need not bound c. Consequently the compact finite-radius class required by the existence, stability, and convergence arguments is not obtained.
issues.overall_effect: For the full old A2 class, minimizer existence, stability, and the uniform coefficient-cost compactness needed for Tikhonov convergence are not guaranteed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retype φ as a scalar map from [0,∞) to [0,∞) and require it to be continuous, nondecreasing, and level-coercive, meaning φ(t) tends to infinity as t tends to infinity. Every finite bound on φ(cρn(f)) then gives a finite bound on cρn(f) through the generalized inverse and hence a finite outer-coefficient radius; use these bounds throughout existence, stability, joint convergence, and the rate argument.
issues.why_classification: The scalar type correction is forced, but coercivity is an additional mathematical premise: the old class coherently included bounded increasing penalties such as 1−exp(−t), for which coefficient sublevels are uncontrolled. Excluding that genuine penalty regime is a substantive but limited restriction. The full Tikhonov chain survives with the same conclusions and rates through a contained repair, so the issue is moderate rather than minor or serious.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: $\varphi:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ is continuous, nondecreasing, and satisfies $\varphi(t)\to\infty$ as $t\to\infty$.

issues.title: Missing alpha factor in Tikhonov sublevel estimates
issues.failure_explanation: By Tikfunc, the objective is D+alpha P. The existence and stability proofs instead use D+P and infer P no larger than the objective. For alpha below one this inequality is false. The correct estimate is alpha P no larger than the objective, or equivalently P no larger than the objective divided by alpha.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the coefficient-radius bounds in the existence and stability proof are invalid, so the compactness chain used by the later Tikhonov results is not formally established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restore the factor α in every Tikhonov sublevel calculation in the existence and stability proofs. From Tα(f,g)≤C infer αP(f)≤C and hence P(f)≤C/α, and define the resulting finite coefficient radii with this factor. Carry the same scaling through the compactness estimates used by convergencerate and corollary1.
issues.why_classification: The old proof makes a genuinely false inequality when α<1, so this is not merely typographical under the severity standard. However, the objective uniquely determines the correction, and inserting the factor only changes fixed-α constants and radius bounds. It requires no new lemma or weakening and preserves every affected statement and rate, making it a minor issue.

issues.title: Fixed-width compactness does not prove the joint Tikhonov limit

failure_location.quote: By (b), the family $\{f_{n,k}\}_{k\in\mathbb{N}}$ is bounded in $\mathcal{B}_1$ and hence relatively compact in $L^2(\Omega)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The convergence claim is asymptotic in both width n and noise index k, whereas the cited stability result begins with n and alpha fixed. Fixed-width subsequences and bounds depending on n do not yield a single subsequence when n tends to infinity. The old proof also passes to an alleged Barron-space limit before establishing varying-width compactness and lower semicontinuity of the Barron norm.
issues.overall_effect: The joint-limit convergence to an R-minimizing solution is not established, so the later use of that convergence to enter the local variational-source neighborhood is also unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a varying-width compactness and lower-semicontinuity lemma: networks whose empirical representation costs are uniformly bounded have a subsequence converging in C(K), hence in L2(Ω), to a Barron function whose Barron norm is at most the liminf of those costs. Rewrite well-posedness(c) for an arbitrary joint sequence (nℓ,kℓ) tending to infinity, use the uniform cost estimate to apply this lemma, and identify the limit as an R-minimizing solution. The rate theorem and corollary may then use this joint convergence to enter the local source-condition neighborhood.
issues.why_classification: Fixed-width stability cannot be diagonalized into the claimed joint limit with bounds depending on n. A complete repair requires a genuine new varying-width compactness/lower-semicontinuity lemma and a substantial replacement of the limit argument. That work is nontrivial but remains contained within the compactness step and recovers the same minimizing-solution and downstream rate guarantees without major loss or global proof reconstruction, so the issue is moderate.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: Let $\{(n_\ell,k_\ell)\}_{\ell=1}^{\infty}$ be any sequence such that $n_\ell\to\infty, k_\ell\to\infty$.

issues.title: Convergence-rate theorem omits the Tikhonov parameter regime

failure_location.quote: According to Theorem~\ref{well-posedness}(c), we have $f_{n,\alpha}^{\delta}\to f^{\dagger}$ in $L^2(\Omega)$ as $\delta\to0$ and $n\to\infty$

issues.failure_explanation: The old theorem claims subsequential convergence as n tends to infinity and delta tends to zero without quantifying alpha. Its proof invokes well-posedness(c), whose convergence conclusion requires alpha tending to zero and alpha^{-1}(delta+n^{-s/2}) tending to zero. Fixed alpha or an alpha that decays too rapidly is allowed by the old rate theorem but lies outside the invoked result's hypotheses.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem's preliminary convergence assertion and its use of the local variational source condition are valid only along admissible regularization-parameter choices, not for arbitrary minimizers indexed merely by n and delta.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add to convergencerate the joint parameter assumptions α→0 and α⁻¹(δ+n⁻ˢᐟ²)→0 as δ→0 and n→∞. State its subsequential convergence and use of the local variational source condition only along such admissible parameter paths, consistently with the hypotheses of well-posedness(c).
issues.why_classification: Importing the missing regime is a short repair and leaves the displayed error estimates and standard rate choices intact. It nevertheless removes the coherent and natural fixed-α and excessively fast-decay regimes allowed by the old theorem, changing a central quantifier on the regularization parameter. The surviving theorem is recognizably the same convergence-rate result, so this limited substantive weakening is moderate.

issues.title: Unsupported EIT H1-Lipschitz claim

failure_location.quote: which demonstrates that the forward map $A$ is locally Lipschitz at $f^\dagger$ with respect to the $H^1(\Omega)$ norm.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: By applying Alessandrini’s identity in conjunction with standard energy estimates (cf. \cite{Alessandrini1990}), one obtains a local Lipschitz estimate~-- in fact, a global one within the uniformly elliptic $L^\infty$ class~-- with respect to the $L^\infty$-norm.
We assume that the true conductivity $f^{\dagger}$ and all admissible conductivities $f$ belong to $W^{1, \infty}(\Omega)$ and satisfy uniform ellipticity bounds $0<\alpha \leq f(x) \leq \beta$.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims a uniform local Lipschitz estimate with respect to the H1 norm for all uniformly elliptic W1-infinity conductivities, with a constant depending only on the neighborhood and domain. The old paper actually establishes an L-infinity-based estimate and assumes only individual W1-infinity membership, not a common W1-infinity bound. In two dimensions, H1 does not uniformly control L-infinity on that class; the required interpolation contains a W1-infinity factor. The supported replacement therefore requires a uniformly bounded class and gives exponent 1/2 rather than 1.
issues.overall_effect: The EIT example does not justify using Hölder exponent 1 in the paper's abstract ENN estimates. The corrected exponent changes the associated sufficient-width order from delta^{-2} to delta^{-4} and restricts the admissible conductivity class.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the H1-Lipschitz assertion by the supported estimate on a uniformly elliptic class with a common W1,∞ bound. Combine the standard L∞-Lipschitz estimate for the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map with the two-dimensional Gagliardo–Nirenberg inequality to obtain local H1-Hölder continuity of exponent 1/2 in the standard operator norm from H1/2(∂Ω) to H−1/2(∂Ω). Use θ=1/2 in the abstract ENN estimate, giving sufficient width of order δ⁻⁴ rather than δ⁻².
issues.why_classification: The correction requires both a uniform W1,∞ restriction and a genuine weakening from exponent 1 to exponent 1/2, with a corresponding deterioration of the advertised width order. These are meaningful changes, so the defect is not minor. The same EIT forward map still satisfies a recognizable version of the abstract Hölder hypothesis through a short standard interpolation argument, however, so the loss and repair remain limited rather than serious.
